news.title: The World Cup Didn't Change Norway. It Changed How the World Noticed Norway.
news.lede: For years, Norway had a branding challenge that most countries would envy: people liked Norway, they just didn't think about it very often. Then came the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Suddenly, millions of people around the world were talking about Norwegian football, Erling Braut Haaland, Viking “Row” celebrations, salmon, brown cheese and the values Norway represents. The tournament became much more than a sporting event.

news.title: Updated: England Rugby’s World Cup-winning captain Johnson to attend Malta-Germany clash on Saturday
news.lede: The Malta Rugby Football Union will have a special guest for Saturday’s Rugby Europe Trophy Division clash against Germany, as England’s World Cup-winning captain, Martin Johnson, is expected to attend at the Tony Bezzina Stadium. Byron Camilleri, the Minister for Education and Sport, made the announcement during a press conference at the Tony Bezzina Stadium, during which details of Saturday’s Trophy Division clash were announced. The Malta rugby national team enjoyed an impressive start to their Trophy Division campaign, coming back from 17-0 down to beat Denmark 36-17 last weekend. Next up for Malta is a clash against group favourites Germany in Corradino on Saturday, and the match has special significance as it will be Malta’s 100th international match.

news.title: Soccer-Former Brazil captain Cafu says Neymar leaves proud legacy as Ancelotti begins rebuild
news.lede: SAO PAULO, Nov 4 (Reuters) - ⁠Former Brazil captain Cafu said Neymar's international career should be remembered as a successful ⁠and honourable one after the forward retired from the national team following Brazil's disappointing ‌World Cup campaign this year. Neymar, Brazil's all-time leading scorer, said in late July that he no longer wanted to play for the national team, weeks after suggesting his international career had ended following Brazil's last-16 defeat by Norway at the ​World Cup. "The end of the cycle with the national team ⁠comes for everyone," Cafu, Brazil's most-capped player ⁠with 150 appearances, told Reuters on Tuesday. "The most important thing is that his cycle was a ⁠successful ‌one.
